A 68-year-old woman with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and heart failure on a loop diuretic is admitted with an exacerbation. The monitor shows frequent premature ventricular contractions (early, wide, bizarre QRS complexes with no P wave). Oxygen saturation is 86%, potassium 2.9 mEq/L (normal 3.5-5.0) and magnesium 1.3 mg/dL (normal 1.7-2.2). Which is the next step?

A 25-year-old man with asthma is brought in after a stab wound to the left chest. His blood pressure is 78/50 mm Hg, his neck veins are distended and his heart sounds are muffled (Beck triad). Bedside ultrasound shows pericardial fluid compressing the heart. Intravenous fluids are running. Which treatment does this traumatic tamponade need next?

A 67-year-old man with hypertension has 3 weeks of low fevers to 38.2 °C (100.8 °F), fatigue and weight loss. He now has a holosystolic murmur; he had no murmur before, and echocardiography confirms new mitral regurgitation without a vegetation. Two blood cultures drawn more than 12 hours apart both grow Enterococcus faecalis, and no other source of infection is found. Which modified Duke classification fits?

The day after a cardiac catheterization through the right femoral artery, a 66-year-old woman with obesity and hypertension has a tender swelling at the puncture site. Ultrasound shows a 1.5 cm blood-filled cavity outside the artery wall that communicates with the arterial lumen. Which is the most appropriate management?

A 74-year-old woman with hypertension and stable angina takes metoprolol and diltiazem. Her electrocardiogram shows a regular rhythm at 64 beats per minute, one P wave before every narrow QRS and a constant PR interval of 0.26 s. She has no fatigue, shortness of breath, palpitations or heart failure symptoms. Which is the appropriate management?

A 55-year-old man with hypertension has worsening exertional dyspnea and leg swelling. A 24-hour monitor shows premature ventricular contractions making up 22% of his beats (about 24,000 per day), and echocardiography shows a new cardiomyopathy with no other cause found, attributed to the premature beats. Which treatment fits?

A 74-year-old man with ischemic heart disease and sick sinus syndrome has spells of near-fainting. Ambulatory monitoring shows tachy-brady syndrome (fast rhythms alternating with slow rhythms and pauses), and the fast episodes are runs of ventricular tachycardia that match his symptoms. Which device does he need?

A 45-year-old woman with a recent viral illness has acute pericarditis: sharp substernal chest pain relieved by leaning forward, a pericardial friction rub (a superficial scratchy sound) and widespread ST elevation. She has a documented contraindication to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. She is afebrile without an effusion. Which regimen fits?
